body_ar: الحمد لله رب العالمين وأصلي وأسلم على من بعث رحمة للعالمين ، وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن اهتدى بهديه واستن بسنته إلى يوم الدين ، أما بعد، فإن الإنسان يسير إلى مستقر له هو لاقيه لا محالة فعليه أن يتدبر فيما أمامه وأن يتذكر تلك المشاهد التي تنتظره لأن ذلك مدعاة للإعداد لها ، ولذلك فإن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم خرج في جنازة ، فلما وضع الميت في قبره نظر إلى أصحابه ، فقال: "أي إخواني أعدوا لمثل هذه الضجعة".
body_en:
All praise belongs to God, Lord of the worlds, and I ask God to bless and grant peace to the one who was sent as a mercy to all the worlds, and to his family, his Companions, and all who follow his guidance and keep to his sunnah until the Day of Judgement.

To proceed: a human being is travelling towards a resting place of his own which he will meet without fail, so he must reflect on what lies ahead of him and call to mind those scenes that are waiting for him, because that is what prompts a person to prepare for them. It was for this that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out with a funeral, and when the dead man had been placed in his grave he looked at his Companions and said: 'My brothers, prepare for a lying-down like this one.'

flags.context: فلما وضع الميت في قبره نظر إلى أصحابه ، فقال: "أي إخواني أعدوا لمثل هذه الضجعة"
options: prepare for a lying-down like this one
make ready for a resting place such as this
prepare yourselves for a bed like this one
flags.note: الضجعة is the act or posture of lying down on one's side, pointing at the body just laid in the grave. 'Resting place' reads better but shifts the image from the posture to the place. The Sheikh gives no narrator or collection for the report, and none has been supplied.

translator_notes: The published page carries only the opening excerpt of this lecture/sermon; the Arabic breaks off mid-sentence and the full text is offered on the site as a downloadable Word document. The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends. Nothing has been supplied to complete it.
The excerpt gives only the opening framing of the lecture; none of the 'scenes' named in the title is described in the written source.
